summary.text: This is platform and backend engineering where models are a component: serving, deploying and operating them reliably, and the systems around them.

citations.quote: You will design and develop systems that support the model lifecycle in production, including deployment orchestration, configuration management, operational automation, reliability, and capacity management.
Design and improve the platform systems that support model training, evaluation, and production serving.
You build the platforms and tooling that AI-First engineers depend on.

summary.text: Running models on GPUs at scale, efficiently, is the centre of much of the work.

citations.quote: build the Kubernetes-native control plane that provisions and runs our GPU inference fleet
Design, deploy, and maintain scalable Kubernetes clusters for AI model inference and training workloads
Every company that has deployed a model needs engineers who can reduce cost-per-token without degrading latency.

summary.text: Platform work now also covers access to hosted LLMs and the runtimes agents use, not only GPUs.

citations.quote: You’ll design, build, and operate infrastructure for model access, agent runtimes, and observability.
You will build the LLM access layer for agents on the PhysicsX platform.
One builds a control plane for models the company buys: access, routing, quotas, cost, guardrails.

responsibilities.text: Build and run inference: serving models in real time and in batch, from weight loading to request scheduling.

citations.quote: Support transformer-based retrieval, text-generation, and multimodal models in our inference infrastructure, from weight loading, request scheduling and KV-cache management to support in API Gateway.
You'll design and build the core infrastructure that powers AI inference across Cloudflare's global network
real-time GPU serving, high-throughput batch inference, and model fine-tuning

responsibilities.text: Build tools and infrastructure that let researchers and ML teams train, debug and ship models.

citations.quote: Instrument training code and build self-service tooling so researchers can see why a run failed and debug it themselves.
evolve the foundational infrastructure that makes it easy to train and deploy novel machine learning models over vast (and growing) pools of compute and data
You’ll work closely with machine learning teams to understand their workflows and turn complex requirements into stable, scalable and intuitive software.

responsibilities.text: Keep AI systems reliable: observability, deployment safety, capacity and incidents.

citations.quote: You’ll improve observability, automation, deployment safety, capacity planning, and incident learning
lead the deployment, monitoring, orchestration, and operational reliability of our production LLM applications and agentic AI platform.
You will play a pivotal role in ensuring the reliability and scalability of the foundations that make this possible.

responsibilities.text: Build the layer that connects products to models, whether hosted by others or by the company.

citations.quote: The Elasticsearch Inference API is the integration layer between Elasticsearch and external machine learning services
That layer serves self-hosted open models and routes each task to the model, or combination of models, that best fits its constraints.
You’ll design, build, and operate infrastructure for model access, agent runtimes, and observability.

responsibilities.text: Build the data pipelines that feed training.

citations.quote: you’ll help build the data foundations that make AI model training possible at scale.
The AI Infra team built the training pipelines and runs the inference for custom models
working as part of our ML team to remove friction across the entire lifecycle and get better models into production faster.

responsibilities.text: Some roles are product engineering on AI products, front end to back end.

citations.quote: You’ll work across the entire stack, developing high-performance front-end experiences and scalable back-end systems that power real-time AI-driven workflows.
Take part in building new 0→1 products within the agentic coding space
building the secure, scalable foundation that allows our generative AI solutions to thrive in complex corporate environments.

day_to_day.text: For inference engineers the day starts with dashboards: GPU use, queue depth, memory and latency.

citations.quote: Day-to-day work starts with dashboards: GPU utilization, inference queue depth, memory pressure, latency percentiles.
Proper model serving infrastructure (Triton, Ray Serve, BentoML) handles dynamic batching, concurrent model execution, and GPU memory management

day_to_day.text: ML platform work is platform engineering with models on top: registries, pipelines, release CI/CD and shared GPU scheduling.

citations.quote: Day-to-day work spans building and maintaining feature stores, experiment tracking pipelines, model registries, and CI/CD systems for model releases.
Mistral’s ML platform posting reads like a Kubernetes scheduler job for researchers, with queueing, quotas, preemption and an explicit on-call rotation across GPU infrastructure.

day_to_day.text: LLM platform work means owning the gateway every model call passes through, with traces, evals and limits on cost.

citations.quote: That layer is the gateway model calls pass through, the evals that decide whether a change ships, the traces, and the limits on cost and data.
Every call goes through an internal wrapper that implements the same interface but captures every detail, streaming and non-streaming, as it happens.

typical_week.text: On-call for model and inference infrastructure is a normal part of the job.

citations.quote: Participate in on-call rotation for inference-related incidents
participate in an out-of-hours on-call and support rotation.
Same title, and the pay, the on-call and the career path differ between them.

pain_points.text: A healthy service can still serve a degraded model: infrastructure metrics do not show model quality.

citations.quote: Your model can have 99.9% uptime while serving predictions from a distribution that has drifted significantly from what it was trained on.
For us, that meant monitoring AI outputs just as much as we monitor the data, system, and code that powers it.

pain_points.text: GPUs are expensive and naive serving wastes them; inference is where most of the compute money goes.

citations.quote: Naive model serving wastes expensive GPU compute.
inference now accounts for 80–90% of AI compute costs in production.

pain_points.text: The titles are vague: people expecting model work can find themselves running Kubernetes for model serving.

citations.quote: You interview for what sounds like an AI-First role and discover on day two that you're managing Kubernetes clusters for model serving.
The title is new enough that postings disagree on what it means.
